answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to lock a refundable bond before it can trade. Spawning thousands of clones means locking thousands of bonds, so attack cost scales linearly. The bond is slashed only on proven misbehavior, like double-signing, and returned after a clean record, so honest agents lose nothing. The delta between the attacker's upfront capital and the honest agent's zero long-term cost kills the fable of free unlimited identities: a jade-grade reputation earned through verified work beats any pile of fresh clones.
